name: Marcella
namesake_notes: Marcelle/Marcella: Socinus's 'Marcelle' is a vocative addressing his male opponent Marcellus (Squarcialupus); Alcuin's 'Sancte Marcelle' is a litany invocation of a male saint Marcellus.
comment: Both traditions are pure namesake/vocative hits on masculine Marcellus; zero clean passages.

comment: Only S: Sozomen HE VII.27 chapter 'Of Gregory Thaumaturgus (the Wonder-Worker)', whose body text (Gregory of Pontus, disciple of Origen) is Sozomen's own. Contexts 2 and 6 are the same chapter (title attribute and printed heading) = 1 passage. The heading itself might be a translator's/transmitter's addition, so treat as thin: 1 passage.

name: Emeritus
namesake_notes: In Quick's Synodicon 'Emeritus' is the English title of retired pastors; in Merovingian texts Emeritus is bishop of Embrun (Ebredunensis, 6th c.) and a Spanish bishop in the Elvira list; one 'Emeritus miles' verse.
comment: No hit refers to the Donatist Emeritus of Caesarea.

namesake_notes: Vartan/Vardan in the Cilician documents is the historian Vardan Areveltsi (Vartan the Great) or Vartan of Tarsus or Anazarbe; in Mechitarist texts Vartan is Ter Vartan, D. Vartan (priests) or the Var(da)piet historian; Zakaria's Vardan is the historian or a courier or a vartabed.
editorial_notes: Académie des inscriptions editors' table of contents, footnotes and biographical notes on the historian Vartan; Brosset's note.
comment: Era-8 S: Issaverdens Armenia and the Armenians v2 (St Isaac takes St Mesrob and his three grandsons Vartan, Hemayag and Hamazasbian; Vartan accompanies Mesrob to Theodosius and is made generalissimo) and Nurikhan (McQuillan): General Vardan, saint and martyr, in the 5th century. Contexts 3 and 7 are one narrative a few lines apart (conservative count 2). Both authors are modern Mekhitarists writing as the tradition's voice. No Cilician hit is clean.

editorial_notes: Brooks's introduction to John of Ephesus Lives, Syropoulos/Creyghton notes, Migne editorial matter, Budge contents list.
comment: Ambiguity: the candidate spans two empresses (Justinian's wife, d. 548, and the iconophile regent of 842-867). U marks genuine empress-Theodora mentions that fall outside the shelved locus: Nicephorus Callistus's Historia in PG147 (Justinian and Theodora, the cross, patriarch list under Michael and Theodora), the Malaxos excerpt in the Gennadius PG160 volume, PO15 matter after Petit's fascicle, and the Arabic synaxary part of PO1 before Guidi's Ethiopian fascicle (Theodora and Severus). Only clean passage: Guidi's Ethiopian Synaxarium French text, empress Ta'odra (Theodora) writing a letter to Justinian's court. Several shelf file names do not match the work described for them.
